interactions.summary: Greg briefly compares China's patronage logic to America, gives Jiang's biographical setup, and asks what reforms he wanted in Chinese education and how Chinese and Western systems differ in breaking people down.

Jiang says China and the West are converging more than he once thought, explains his attempt to cultivate individuality and agency in students, and says the Great Books work best when they awaken a divine spark in each student rather than impose bureaucratic schooling reforms from above.
Greg affirms Jiang's educational project as a kind of Trojan horse for self-actualization, then pivots from education into Jiang's claims that power runs on narrative and financial alchemy.
Jiang begins the alchemy answer by saying American power rests on faith in the dollar after the break with gold convertibility.

speaker_notes.note: Greg's biographical recap is garbled and repetitive near the Yale line, but the functional move is clear: he is setting up Jiang's educational authority before asking about reform.

claims.claim: Jiang says the differences between China and the West are no longer as stark as he once believed because the two cultures are converging.
Jiang says his main educational concern in China was cultivating individuality and agency so students would believe they possess an eternal soul with its own vocation and delight.
claims.temporal_scope: Retrospective statement made on 2025-10-07 about Jiang's educational mission.

claims.claim: Jiang says he built China's first public-school international program on an American liberal-arts model, with an English library, seminar classes, and a daily newspaper, to create a space for individual agency.
Jiang says that reform effort failed largely because parents wanted to micromanage their children rather than support the cultivation of autonomous agency.

Jiang says teaching Great Books directly to high-school students has been more successful because authors like Plato, Homer, Dante, and Shakespeare can awaken a spark of agency at the individual level.
Jiang says the purpose of the Great Books, especially Homer and Dante, is to remind people that a divine spark in them remains connected to the higher good.
Jiang says the power of the U.S. dollar as global reserve currency now rests on faith and trust in the American state rather than convertibility into gold.
Jiang says Bretton Woods created a gold-backed dollar order in 1945, but after Nixon ended gold convertibility in 1971 the system became a kind of financial alchemy.
claims.temporal_scope: Historical monetary claim made on 2025-10-07 about 1945 and 1971.

signature_moments.moment: Education should make the soul shine in the world rather than merely train compliant performers.
signature_moments.source_phrase: make the soul shine in the world
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It condenses Jiang's deepest educational aim into one memorable formulation that later read-writing should preserve.

signature_moments.moment: The Great Books are not just curriculum; they are reminders that a divine spark still links a person to the higher good.
signature_moments.source_phrase: there's a divine spark in them
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It explains why Jiang treats Homer and Dante as civilizational repair tools rather than prestige reading lists.

signature_moments.moment: After gold ended, the dollar became alchemy: a world order floating on faith in American continuity.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the pivot from Jiang's educational anthropology to his monetary theory of power.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The student's sense of being a real person with a soul, vocation, and power to direct a life rather than merely obey a system.
Jiang's name for the inner source of soul, agency, and orientation toward the higher good that great books can reawaken.
The post-1945 monetary arrangement Jiang invokes as the last period when the dollar's authority was openly tied to gold rather than pure belief.

chronology_notes.note: This packet ties together two dated arcs: Jiang says his current four-year Great Books phase came after an earlier failed reform program, and he dates the monetary shift from gold-backed dollars to post-1971 financial faith.

uncertainty_notes.note: The transcript clips Greg's biography setup and his appreciative interjection after 'divine spark,' but the educational argument and transition into monetary alchemy remain clear.
